# Ray-Primitive Intersection (Analytic/Geometric)

Also called: Analytic Ray-Primitive Intersection, Closed-form Ray Intersection, Geometric Ray Tracing

## Overview
This family computes exact intersection parameters for rays against standard geometric primitives (spheres, planes, triangles, tetrahedra) by solving their implicit or parametric algebraic equations [G]. It avoids iterative root-finding loops used in [Ray-Marching](52-ray-marching.md) or [Implicit Surface and SDF Intersection](2795-implicit-surface-and-sdf-intersection.md), and handles specific primitive shapes rather than axis-aligned bounding volumes like [Ray-Volume and Bounding Box Intersection](10057-ray-volume-and-bounding-box-intersection.md) [G]. It serves as the foundational geometric primitive test for ray tracing and volume rendering pipelines [G].

## Shared principles
The shared principles of this family are the geometric definition of rays and the parallel execution model [G].
**Ray Definition**
Rays are defined by an origin $\mathbf{o}$ and a direction $\mathbf{d}$ [G]. The direction is typically normalized. The origin is often the camera eye position, but can vary based on the camera model [G].
**Parallel Execution**
Computations are mapped to parallel threads [G]. Each thread typically processes one or more pixels or samples [G]. Memory access patterns are optimized for coalescing [G]. Synchronization is used to manage data dependencies between threads [G].

## Subtopics

### [Sphere Intersection](1620-sphere-intersection.md)
Computes entry and exit $t$-values for a ray intersecting a sphere, returning sentinel values on failure. It is chosen for volumetric spheres and simple scene geometry where quadratic solutions are efficient. It differs from [Ray-Triangle Intersection](11312-ray-triangle-intersection.md) by computing path length through a participating medium rather than discrete surfaces.

### [Ray-Tetrahedron Intersection](2525-ray-tetrahedron-intersection.md)
Determines the entry and exit points of a ray traversing a tetrahedral cell, the fundamental primitive for unstructured volumetric data. It is chosen for rendering unstructured grids and finite element analysis. It differs from [Ray-Plane/Rectangle Intersection](6498-ray-plane-rectangle-intersection.md) by handling closed volume constraints and shared edge computations.

### [Ray-Plane/Rectangle Intersection](6498-ray-plane-rectangle-intersection.md)
Computes intersections with planar primitives, ranging from infinite planes to bounded rectangles. It is chosen for bounding volumes, ground planes, and surface hit testing. It differs from curved primitives like [Sphere Intersection](1620-sphere-intersection.md) by relying on linear algebra and plane equations.

### [Ray-Triangle Intersection](11312-ray-triangle-intersection.md)
Computes the intersection of a ray with a single triangle, determining if the ray hits the interior and returning the distance. It is chosen for polygonal surface rendering and mesh geometry. It differs from [Sphere Intersection](1620-sphere-intersection.md) and [Ray-Plane/Rectangle Intersection](6498-ray-plane-rectangle-intersection.md) by explicitly testing against a finite, arbitrary triangular surface using barycentric coordinate validation.
